headline: Last session: Sensex dropped over 570 points and Nifty tanked to 22,421 amid heavy FPI selling.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed for trading today due to an NSE holiday. It will reopen on Monday, 5 October.

why: Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) pulled out a record Rs 3 lakh crore from Indian equities over 9 months.
US Treasury yield surged to a multi-year high of 5.34%, dampening demand for emerging market assets.
India's 10-year bond yield breached 7.20%, reaching a 2.5-year high.
Surging crude oil prices and global rate hikes triggered aggressive foreign capital outflows.
whatHappening: Indian stock markets are closed today, October 2, for Gandhi Jayanti and will reopen on Monday, October 5.
D-Street benchmark shares logged their longest weekly losing streak in 25 years.
The Indian Rupee sank to 96.31, marking its biggest single-day decline in over two months.
Vishakha Renewables filed preliminary IPO papers aiming to raise Rs 1,250 crore.
summary: Indian equities are closed today, October 2, in observance of Gandhi Jayanti. In the last trading session, benchmark indices extended losses to mark their longest weekly losing streak in 25 years amidst heavy foreign outflows. Trading will resume on Monday, October 5.
